# Wadi

> Wadi (https://wadi.house) is an AI-native parametric home designer. A house is authored in Wadi's `.wdl` design language and rendered live as a 3D model, 2D floor plans, elevations, and dimensioned drawings. The app is built so that an AI agent can author the house directly.

There are two ways for an agent to drive Wadi.

## For an in-browser agent (runs JavaScript on the page)

The viewer at https://wadi.house/app exposes a `window.wadi` API. Call `await window.wadi.help()` on the page for a self-contained primer.

**Keep the model visible.** The WDL editor and configurator panels auto-hide when you apply a change (`setWdl` / `chooseTemplate`), so the user watches the 3D model change rather than code or knobs — this matters in a small embedded browser. Leave them hidden; call `window.wadi.setPanels(true)` to reveal them and `false` to hide again (the user can also reopen them with the on-screen tabs).

**Work with the user one step at a time.** Do not do everything in one shot and leave the user to fix your guesses. When a request involves a choice — which template, how many rooms and their sizes, the layout, roof style, where the stairs go, add vs. move a room — present two or three concrete options and ask the user to pick before applying anything. Make one meaningful change per step, show the result, and confirm before the next. Prefer small, reversible edits over regenerating the whole house, and state any assumption you had to make so the user can correct it.

**Strongly prefer editing a template over building from scratch.** Authoring a whole house from a blank `.wdl` is error-prone (wall alignment across floors, roof sizing, cantilever support, plinth, staircase). Start from the ready-made home closest to what the user wants and change it:

- `await window.wadi.listTemplates()` — ready-made homes: `[{id, title, meta}]`. Pick the closest.
- `await window.wadi.chooseTemplate(id)` — load it as your starting point.
- `await window.wadi.getTemplateWdl(id)` — READ another home's `.wdl` WITHOUT loading it, to study how it does a roof/staircase/grid/etc. This leaves the user's current model untouched — use it to look things up instead of loading an example just to peek (only `chooseTemplate` when you actually want to start from that home).
- `await window.wadi.getWdl()` — read its `.wdl` (the single source of truth).
- Edit the text: resize, rename, add/remove rooms; prefer adjusting a parametric template's variables (the whole house re-flows) over rewriting geometry.
- `await window.wadi.setWdl(wdl)` — compile and load live. On a compile/schema error returns `{ok:false, errors:[…]}` and leaves the model unchanged; on success returns the structural check (`{loaded:true, errors, warnings, summary}`) — **read it and fix warnings before telling the user it is ready.**
- `await window.wadi.checkWdl(wdl)` — optional dry-run compile.
- `window.wadi.captureView()` — a JPEG data URL of the current 3D view.
- `window.wadi.listRooms()` / `enterRoom(key)` / `exitRoom()` — first-person interior views.

Only build from scratch if no template fits. If you must, follow this order and re-check as you go: plinth on the lowest floor → ground-floor rooms + a slab per floor → upper floors laid over the floor below with walls ALIGNED to those beneath (only small partitions may lack support) + a slab → pillars under any cantilever (a pillar that carries a slab OR a staircase landing above it must reach it — a short one is flagged, C25; a pillar supporting only the roof, or with nothing above, is fine) → a roof covering the WHOLE top floor → a staircase spanning the floors.

**Roofs.** One roof per area: extend an existing roof's segments (`width`/`end`) to cover more, never add a second roof over an already-covered area (warning C18). Orient each hip segment's ridge along the LONGER side of the footprint — if a segment's span (`width`) exceeds its ridge run (`start`→`end` length) it collapses to a pyramid (warning C17).

**Staircases.** Give a stair enough run to climb in one or two flights; a cramped box forces extra switchback flights (warning C19). After `setWdl`, read `await window.wadi.describeHouse()` — its `staircases` array reports each stair's flight count, climb `direction`, the top-landing rectangle (in project units — where you step onto the floor) with its `facing`, and `min_length_for_1_flight` / `min_length_for_2_flights`. To fix cramped or misdirected stairs: enlarge the box to `min_length_for_2_flights` along its run axis, set `direction` so the top landing faces the room you want to reach, and leave that room's wall open (or add a door) at the landing so there is a way off the stair onto the floor (warning C20). Keep the staircase over the plinth — if you add it at the building edge, extend BOTH the plinth and the floor's slab under it (warnings C21, C24; the slab fills the gap between the stair base and the plinth) — and enclose it in a room of its own footprint OR add pillars under it so the flights and landings are carried (warning C22). Author the steps in THIS model's units: do not copy stair dimensions from another example without rescaling (a model in metres will make the stair absurdly large or small). In the default 10-units-per-foot scale use about `step_rise 6` and `step_tread 10`; the check reports the right values for the current model (warning C23).

Typical loop: `chooseTemplate` → `getWdl` → edit → `setWdl` → fix warnings (and `describeHouse()` for staircases) → repeat.

The same capabilities are also registered as WebMCP tools on `navigator.modelContext` (`wadi_get_wdl`, `wadi_set_wdl`, `wadi_check_wdl`, `wadi_wdl_reference`, and more) for agents that consume WebMCP. Where WebMCP tool-calling is not surfaced, use `window.wadi` directly as above.

## `.wdl` syntax essentials

- A minimal house:

  ```
  house House {
    convention center                 // room x/y/size are wall CENTRELINES, so abutting rooms share a wall (alternative: outer)
    site { plot (400, 300) }          // plot W, L in project units (10 units = 1 ft by default)
    defaults { floor_height 100 wall_height 92 slab_thickness 8 wall_thickness 8 }

    floor 1 "Ground Floor" height 92 slab_thickness 0 {   // floor fields go in the HEADER, before the '{'
      room Living at (0, 0) size (160, 140) material "living" {
        wall north south west
        wall east { door D1 at 55 size (30, 84) }   // a door needs a name; `at` = offset along the wall
      }
      room Kitchen at (160, 0) size (120, 140) { wall north south east }  // west omitted -> open passage to Living
    }

    // A ROOF sits on its OWN floor stacked ABOVE the walls' floor, so it rests on top of them.
    floor 2 "Roof" {
      roof name "Hip" pitched endpoint closed slope height 60 overhang 12 material "roof" {
        segment "s0" from (140, 0) to (140, 140) width 280   // ridge centreline down the 280x140 footprint; width = span
      }
    }
  }
  ```

- Names are BARE identifiers (`room Living`, `door D1`), not quoted. `"strings"` are only for titles/materials.
- Object types inside a floor: `room`, `wall`, `pillar`, `beam`, `slab`, `roof`, `staircase`, `kitchen_platform`, `item` (furniture GLB), `component` (reusable).
- Floor-level fields (`height`, `wall_height`, `slab_thickness`, `enabled`) go in the floor HEADER, before the `{`, for example `floor 1 "Ground" height 92 slab_thickness 0 { … }`. Only object declarations go inside the `{ }` body; putting `slab_thickness 0` in the body is a parse error. Use `slab_thickness 0` so walls sit on the base rather than floating on a slab, and set `height = wall_height + slab_thickness` so the floor above sits flush.
- A ROOF goes on its OWN floor stacked ABOVE the rooms' floor (add a top `floor N "Roof"` and put the `roof` there). A roof on the same floor as the walls renders at floor level, not on top. A `roof` holds one or more `segment` lines (ridge centreline `from`→`to`, `width` = the span). Endpoint style: `pitched endpoint closed` = hip, `pitched endpoint open` = gable, `shed`, `flat`.
- Openings live inside `wall SIDE { … }`: `door NAME at OFFSET size (w,h) [open]`, `window NAME at OFFSET size (w,h) [sill N]`.
- Two rooms are connected when they abut and the shared wall has a door on one room (omitted on the other), or is omitted on both (open passage).
- Coordinates: origin top-left, X right, Y DOWN. Positions/sizes are project units (10 = 1 ft by default).
- Parametric: declare variables and write formulas in any numeric slot; reusable components and the unified `roof` object are supported.

For complete, correct examples, load a template with `chooseTemplate` then read its full `.wdl` with `getWdl`.

## For a coding agent (no browser)

Use the Wadi MCP server (`wadi-mcp`), which bundles the compiler, reference docs, and a rasteriser so an agent can check, preview, and reference `.wdl` files without the repository. Tools include `wadi_check`, `wadi_preview`, `wadi_reference`, `wadi_scope`, and `wadi_view_3d`.
